current_date: Approved by Planning Committee 11 November 2020 (consulted 14 Sep - 28 Oct 2020), per the council's Local Checklists page text as captured in the data file; the PDF itself carries no date
current_evidence: The PDF works and is the 'Local Requirements, what is required and when' document linked from the council's Local Checklists page, and two searches found no newer NFDC list (only the separate New Forest NPA July 2026 list). The live council pages returned client errors and the democracy site blocks fetching, so it could not be confirmed that no post-2020 revision exists. A planning.data.gov.uk record gives a start date of 2024-01-01 but links only the same checklist page.

issues.detail: Householder (32 rows) and Outline (24 of 30 rows) list almost every row label from the 'Summary of Local Requirements by Application Type' matrix, ignoring the Yes/No values in each column. Householder therefore includes items the source does not apply to householders: Affordable Housing Statement (10+ units), Community Involvement Statement (major only), Retail Impact Assessment, Rural Workers' Dwelling, Mineral Resource Assessment, Nutrient budget (net new dwellings), Viability Appraisal (major), SuDS Strategy (10+ units, >0.5 ha or 1,000 sqm), Environmental Statement and Sustainability Statement (householder explicitly exempt). In addition, 27 Full planning rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', and the telecoms statement is filed under 'Change of use - prior approval' although Part 16 telecoms prior approval is not a change of use.
issues.evidence: Source item 25 Sustainability Statement: exempt 'householder works'; item 1 Affordable Housing: 10 or more units; item 6 Community Involvement: major development

issues.detail: Householder and Outline trigger excerpts are bare matrix labels with stray Yes/No cells and the next row number, so they state no trigger. Examples: 'Affordable Housing Statement 2.', 'Air Quality Assessment No No No No Yes* Yes*...', 'Parking Provision 20.'. Off-by-one row merges also give the same excerpt to different requirements: Arboricultural and Viability both read 'Tree Survey /Arboricultural Statement 32 Viability Appraisal 33.', and Nutrient Neutrality and Minerals both read 'Nutrient budget... 17.Mineral Resource assessment...'.
issues.evidence: Summary_Checklist.pdf matrix rows as excerpted in app_type_rows

issues.detail: Full planning excerpts are often the wrong text or are cut off. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' shows Arboricultural Method Statement text. 'Viability' runs into '2.Archaeological Desk-based...', and 'Travel Plan' runs into '31.Tree Survey'. 'Drainage Strategy' ('accompanied by a drainage strategy.') drops the 10+ units / >0.5 ha / 1,000 sqm threshold. 'Planning Statement' says it 'can be submitted with any planning application' but the trigger is major applications, departures and proposals needing detailed policy consideration. 'Design and Access Statement' is legislative boilerplate. 'Heritage Statement' is a web reference. Real thresholds are missing: Retail Impact (>1,000 sqm GIA outside town centres, >500 sqm in villages/outside built-up areas) and Renewable and Low Carbon Energy Statement (new floorspace >100 sqm or 1+ dwellings).
issues.evidence: Items 7, 20, 22, 26, 30, 32 of 'Local Requirements - when/what types of application information will be required'

issues.detail: Local requirements with no app-type row: High Speed Broadband statement (all new residential development); Green Belt Openness Statement (development affecting Green Belt openness); and Recreational Mitigation Strategy for the New Forest and Solent Coast (50+ homes need on-site ANRG; under 50 homes, or any residential within 5.6 km of the Solent coast, need a financial contribution). Recreational mitigation appears only in fragmentary tab_items. The Telecommunications Statement is not listed for full telecoms applications.
issues.evidence: Items 5, 9 and 21 of the source list; 'All residential development within 5.6km of the Solent coast'

issues.detail: Most tab_items are page furniture, download-link text, checklist form questions or matrix fragments rather than requirements. Examples: 'Local checklists for planning applications... You may need to submit extra information with your .'; 'Our local checklists specify the information...'; download lists ('Summary of Local Requirements by Application Type (PDF, 84 KB)...'; 'Biodiversity Checklist for householders (PDF, 203 KB)...'); the 15-minute Duty Planner advice service; a garbled calculator URL ('mid=POS_ANRG&ebz=1_1598465693608'); a glossary line ('SAC = Special Area of Conservation...'); biodiversity form questions ('YES/NO SECTION 1 - Designated Sites... Please answer ALL questions'); and 'Nutrient budget... No No Yes* Yes*... 17.'
issues.evidence: tab_items from Local-Checklists page, Summary_Checklist.pdf and the Biodiversity checklists

issues.detail: The Nutrient neutrality and Recreational mitigation items each appear about six times in tab_items (page, matrix, summary PDF, minor/major checklists). docs_read lists both the PDF and DOCX versions of each biodiversity checklist.

summary: The link works and points to NFDC's November 2020 local requirements, the newest found, though the live council page could not be fetched to confirm it. Extraction is poor: Householder and Outline rows copy every matrix label regardless of Yes/No, so major-only items appear for householders; triggers are bare labels or merged rows; and broadband, Green Belt and recreational mitigation requirements are missing.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The captured list dates from 2020 and predates the statutory BNG regime (Feb/Apr 2024). Grokbot records a 'Biodiversity Net Gain Report' for Householder (and LBC), but householder applications are now exempt from statutory BNG, so these entries may mislead. The workbook's 'Outdated (>2y)? Yes' flag is correct, and the list should be treated as needing review.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: Source: householder development 'falls within minor development' for BNG; list approved Nov 2020
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The source's own Householder checklist lists "Biodiversity Net gain Report" (raw 17bff642db), so the workbook reflects the source accurately. The real issue is the out-of-date list, which is already flagged Outdated=Yes.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook matches its source, and the list is already flagged as outdated.

withdrawn_issues.detail: List date 2020-11-01 is taken from PDF metadata. The council page text gives the actual approval date as 11 November 2020 (Planning Committee), after consultation from 14 September to 28 October 2020.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: 'reviewed and consulted on between 14 September 2020 and 28 October 2020 and approved by our Planning Committee on 11 November 2020'
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The value is right: the approval on 11 November 2020 (raw 48921d23bd) gives 2020-11-01 at month precision. Only the Date_basis (PDF metadata) could be improved.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
